problem: Facility markers are abstract shapes (triangle, diamond, dot) that do not read as health facilities; a new officer looking at the map cannot tell what the markers stand for.
suggestion: Use a recognisable facility marker (e.g. a building/clinic pin) and say what each marker means in a legend.

problem: There is no overview of the incident situation: the officer cannot see how many incidents are active, how many are critical or warning, or how many have been acknowledged, without counting markers or opening the incidents list. Applies at LGA, state and national level.
suggestion: Summary cards above the map: active incidents, critical, warning, acknowledged/awaiting response, scoped to the user's area.

problem: Facilities with an incident do not stand out on the map: every marker is the same size, and critical (orange) and warning (dark amber) look alike, so the officer cannot see at a glance where the problems are or how serious they are.
suggestion: Red for critical, yellow for warning, larger and drawn on top of normal facilities; normal facilities kept small and quiet.

problem: The side panel runs status counts, a filter, every facility and every mobile unit together in one long list, so problems are hard to pick out from the many normal facilities.
suggestion: Separate the panel into clear sections; show facilities and field teams with incidents first; keep the full list available but secondary.

problem: Every outreach team's logger is listed even when nothing is wrong, which adds noise; a field team with an incident is not shown as an incident.
suggestion: Show field teams with incidents prominently; keep the others available (e.g. collapsed) so T6 can still be done.

problem: The summary cards carry decorative coloured top borders and all-caps labels; they look templated and add visual noise without adding meaning.
suggestion: Strip the borders; plain sentence-case labels; colour only where it means something (critical, warning).

problem: Each entry in the side panel shows too much at once (every incident, its number, age and acknowledgement), so the list is long and hard to scan.
suggestion: Collapsed row per facility: name, where it is (state, LGA, ward) and whether it has an incident; details only when expanded.

problem: Clicking a facility on the map opens a separate card at the top of the panel instead of the facility's own entry in the list, so the pin and the list entry are not visibly the same thing.
suggestion: Clicking a pin expands that facility's row in the list and scrolls to it.

problem: The right of the top bar is untidy: the live indicator, notification bell, user name and role, and sign-out are unevenly spaced, and the bell is an emoji that does not match the rest of the interface.
suggestion: Align the items, use a line icon for notifications to match the interface, group the user's name and sign-out.

problem: The typeface feels plain and basic; a softer, calmer face would suit the interface better.
suggestion: Change the typeface.

problem: Dashed green lines on the map are not explained; the evaluator could not tell what they represent (they are field teams' routes).
suggestion: Add the route line to the legend and label it on the team's card.

problem: Opening an incident replaces the list with a separate detail page, so the officer loses their place and must go back and forth to work through several incidents; the flat list also does not show what needs doing first.
suggestion: List on the left grouped by urgency (awaiting response, escalated, acknowledged), details on the right; selecting an incident keeps the list in view.

problem: The incident details never say in plain words what the problem is: 'What happened' lists the event times, condition, detection time and logger, so the officer has to piece the problem together (which fridge, how warm, for how long, still happening?).
suggestion: A plain-language statement at the top of the details, e.g. 'The ILR at Gwale PHC 2 is too warm: 11.2 °C, above the 8 °C limit, for 2 hours and still rising. Check it now.'

problem: The new 'what is wrong' box and the selected incident row use a thick coloured stripe on one edge, a decorative device that looks templated and adds nothing.
suggestion: Drop the edge stripes; let the severity icon and a soft background carry the colour.

problem: The performance page is a dense table with jargon (MTTA, MTTR) explained in a long paragraph of plain text; there is no overview figure or chart, so it is hard to see at a glance how well incidents are being responded to.
suggestion: A statistics page: headline figures with plain names (average time to respond, average time to resolve), charts, and the table as detail.

problem: Performance can only be grouped by place (facility, LGA, state) or tier, but responsibility lies with people; a supervisor cannot see how the officers responsible for incidents are responding, or which facilities each covers.
suggestion: Add a grouping by responsible officer, showing the facilities each is in charge of.

problem: The "Waiting for a response" column in the full table packs two figures into one cell ("18, longest 4 days"), so it is unclear what the number counts or what "longest" refers to.
suggestion: Split into two labelled columns: incidents not yet acknowledged, and how long the oldest has been waiting.

problem: "Consignment" is supply-chain jargon: the page title and labels do not say in plain words that these are batches of vaccine being carried from a store to an outreach site or facility, or that the page is about who has them.
suggestion: Name the page and its items in plain words, and say what the page is for.

problem: Opening a consignment leaves the list for a separate page, and the list is one flat table that does not show what needs doing first (e.g. a handoff awaiting the user's confirmation); unlike the incidents page.
suggestion: Same pattern as incidents: list grouped by what needs doing, details beside the list.

problem: The consignment details show little: no temperature from its logger, no map of where it is or has been, no linked incidents, and the custody record is a plain list, so the chain of who held it is hard to follow.
suggestion: Show the journey (who held it and when), temperature, last known position and any incidents.

problem: The new consignment form opens inline above the list and pushes it down; the expected transit time must be entered in minutes and "Logger" is not explained.
suggestion: Open the form in a dialog over the page; transit time in hours and minutes; plain field names.

problem: The incident and shipment lists show every item in one long scroll (23 or more in a section), so the page is long and it is hard to keep one's place.
suggestion: Show 15 rows at a time in each section, with controls to move between pages.

problem: There is no way to add a product: the national officer can only edit the limits of existing products, and no other role (including the administrator) can add one.
suggestion: Let the national officer add a product, in a dialog like the new shipment form.

problem: The escalation policy tab is a flat table of database rows ("critical, operational", "Acknowledge by (step 1)", "Next tier up", minutes) that does not explain what happens to an incident or when; the evaluator could not tell how escalation works from it.
suggestion: Show each kind of incident as a sequence in plain words (who is told, and after how long if nobody responds), with times in hours and minutes, editable in place.

problem: On the users, jurisdictions, facilities and devices tabs the form for adding a new one sits open on the page, unlike the dialogs used elsewhere (new shipment, add product), which makes the tabs long and inconsistent.
suggestion: Open each add form from a button (e.g. Add user) in a dialog.

problem: The administration tables show every row in one long list.
suggestion: Show 15 rows at a time, as in the incidents and shipments lists.
